extensions.name: Condition expressions
extensions.proposed_meaning: Conditions use yes/no/unknown with strong Kleene conjunction, disjunction and negation. Yes activates a norm, no deactivates it, unknown retains a potential obligation. Conflict is a separate diagnostic state. No activation result supplies an authorization root.
extensions.completion_work: Define exact AST grammar, typed environment lookup, truth tables, total evaluation and norm-origin preservation; prove source/environment refinement.

extensions.name: Multiple evidence references
extensions.proposed_meaning: Resolve exact bounded evidence references under the chosen profile. Duplicate normalized references count once under the proposed successor set policy. For a criterion, admissible positive only gives yes, negative only no, neither unknown, and both conflict. Unaccepted action/output evidence is inadmissible. Legacy any-positive F0 remains separately versioned.
extensions.completion_work: Freeze reference normalization, limits and policy selection; prove criterion verdicts, duplicate invariance, exact joins and legacy compatibility.

extensions.name: Redelegation
extensions.proposed_meaning: A child use is permitted only within the intersection of all complete independently established ancestor envelopes, gates, windows and unrevoked observations in one domain. Cyclic ancestry is invalid. Missing ancestry is unknown. Child declarations cannot enlarge the root grant.
extensions.completion_work: Specify chain derivation and completeness, lawful scope inclusion, time intersections, cycle diagnostics and authentic grant/revocation providers; prove no privilege amplification.

extensions.name: Fulfillment
extensions.proposed_meaning: The owned exact requirement derivation, rather than a caller-supplied criterion list, determines the complete set. All active mandatory criteria must be yes; potential or conflicting mandatory criteria prevent completion. An empty set is allowed only if the owned derivation yields it. Request fulfillment checks selectors, exclusions, freshness at resolution, budget and output constraints.
extensions.completion_work: Build pair-specific criterion derivations and an explicit request/E03 bridge; prove completeness, selection and evidence admissibility under the pinned policy.

extensions.name: Lifecycle
extensions.proposed_meaning: Every historical relation keeps its original exact witness and frame. Ending, replacement and expiration affect live eligibility through exact qualified transitions; they never rewrite prior history. Continues does not replace. Norm origins and conflicts survive projection. Recursive positive rules use least-fixed-point closure, so an unseeded cycle derives no starting fact.
extensions.completion_work: Define historical/live projections, ending targets and revision applicability; prove monotonic positive closure and preservation, then specify any nonmonotone live-state selection separately.

extensions.name: Checked IR
extensions.proposed_meaning: A typed intermediate representation binds the exact selected definition/policy revision, all references, source digests, normalized qualifier values, frame, criterion derivations and evidence. It contains no executable effect authority. Bounded verification rejects unsupported variants and stale commitments; a well-typed IR is not proof of raw source authenticity.
extensions.completion_work: Specify closed IR grammar and resource limits; prove decode/type/source interpretation bridges and replay correspondence for all implemented constructors.

extensions.name: Independent checker
extensions.proposed_meaning: An independently implemented checker validates the supported proof/certificate language against the exact theory, sources and resource profile. Same-toolchain replay is reproduction, not independent verification. Capability coverage is explicit; unsupported proof constructs remain unsupported, never implicitly accepted.
extensions.completion_work: Finish N11A substantial core/semantic sample and N11B required coverage; document separate implementation trust assumptions and replay disagreements.
